misconceptions.description: Assuming all cognitive load should be reduced
misconceptions.trigger: learner argues that every type of cognitive demand is harmful
misconceptions.feedback: Extraneous load should be minimized, but germane load is productive because it supports schema building. The goal is not zero effort; it is useful effort.

misconceptions.description: Blaming the interface for the inherent complexity of the content
misconceptions.trigger: learner treats all difficulty as an interface problem
misconceptions.feedback: Intrinsic load comes from the subject itself. Designers manage it through sequencing and scaffolding, but they do not eliminate the complexity by layout alone.

misconceptions.description: Reducing schemas to isolated facts rather than structured meaning
misconceptions.trigger: learner describes schema theory as simple memorization only
misconceptions.feedback: Schemas are not just stored facts. They are organized structures that let learners interpret, connect, and transfer knowledge more efficiently.
